terms.grammar: phrase: diplōma, diplōmatis n., with the genitive of ingressus
terms.comment: Our description, on the pattern of the passport, commeātūs diplōma (Traupman 217): a diplōma is an official permit (see licence), and ingressus an entering, used by Pliny of his arrival in his province (in ipsō ingressū meō, Plin. Ep. ad Traj. 17.4, in Lewis & Short).
Morgan–Owens marks it with a query.

sources: Lewis & Short: diploma · Lewis & Short: ingressus · Lewis & Short: licentia
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 217.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. passport: visa.
